conventions: בְּעֵינֵי with a pronominal suffix, where the ASV writes an English verb of judgment in its place (`Thinkest thou` v. 3, `seemeth him` v. 12), is read as one fused unit of the preposition and the construct noun headed on the noun (rules 30, 40, as `רַע בְּעֵינֵי` → `it displease`), the suffix taking the English pronoun written for it; the competing reading that marks the verb `added` and the noun unrepresented was set aside in both verses.

בּוֹא with a bare place noun and no preposition or directive he (`into the land` v. 2, `into the city` and `to Jerusalem` v. 14, `to Helam` v. 16) gives the supplied preposition to the accusative of direction under rule 33, not to the verb under rule 44; where the noun carries a directive he (v. 17 חֵלָאמָה → `to Helam`) the he takes the word under rule 32 and the noun keeps only the name.
report: Read all 46 candidate lemmas end to end and the seven `added` units. No construction is analysed two ways without the ASV licensing the difference: the waw table is the ASV's own connective choices plus apodosis waws left unrendered where the ASV writes no connective (vv. 5, 6, 7, 9, 14, 15, 19); לִקְרַאת fuses to `against` (vv. 9, 10, 17) and splits to `to meet` only where the ASV writes a word for each (v. 5); לִפְנֵי fuses to `before` (vv. 15, 19) and to `at … head` (v. 16); בְּיַד fuses to `by` (v. 2) and splits to `into the hand` (v. 10) on the same one-rendering test.

Chapter-wide judgments that hold across verses: בְּעֵינֵי + suffix is the ASV's matrix verb (`Thinkest` v. 3, `seemeth` v. 12) fused on the construct noun with the suffix taking the pronoun; a bare accusative of direction after בּוֹא takes the supplied preposition (`into the land` v. 2, `into the city`, `to Jerusalem` v. 14, `to Helam` v. 16) while the directive he of v. 17 takes its own `to`; עָרַךְ → `put/set … in array` heads on `array` throughout, with the supplied `them` of vv. 9–10 `added` and the reflexive of v. 17 kept with the verb.

Two verse-internal ties were checked and left as returned with their competing readings noted: v. 9 `was set` kept whole on הָיָה with פְּנֵי unrepresented (the `set` could equally be read as פְּנֵי's rendering), and v. 11 purpose לְ → `and` in `come and help` (corpus aligns לְ to `and` in 32 units; the alternative leaves `and` added).

BSB disagreements (6 waws, 4 object markers, 4 לְ) are all documented convention differences — apodosis waws the ASV leaves unrendered, bare object markers, and dative/resultative לְ the recasting silences (rules 14, 16, 21, 40). None is an error.
No promotion or amendment: nothing this chapter taught is general beyond what rules 30, 32, 33, 40, 44 and 52 already say.
